properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 (SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512, RIPEMD-160) ships as a transitive dependency of the web3 1.10 / hardhat test toolchain. Everything in package.json here is a devDependency — the shipped product is Solidity bytecode — so this is toolchain capability, not application crypto. No call site in the repo's own code; presence is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive test-tooling dependency; the shipped smart-contract product contains no MD5.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available AND exercised — the entire product (EOA account model, permit, EIP-3009 authorizations) depends on secp256k1 ECDSA. Migration is EVM-ecosystem-bound, not changeable unilaterally here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Present because ethers vendors @noble/curves; not used by this application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped tree; elliptic 6.5.4 predates the 2024 signature-validation fixes (CVE-2024-28802, CVE-2024-42461; fixed in 6.6.x) — worth a version bump even without direct use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) ships in @noble/curves@1.1.0's API surface (alongside secp256k1, ed25519, x25519), pulled transitively via web3 1.10 → ethereum-cryptography. The application's actual curve is secp256k1 (Ethereum signing via ethereumjs-util/web3); no P-256 call site exists in this repo. Shor-vulnerable capability present in the shipped library — relevant only if a future dependency starts using it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 ships ECDSA/ECDH for secp256k1, NIST curves and ed25519, present transitively via the web3 toolchain. No ECDH call site in this repo — its crypto surface is Keccak-256 + secp256k1 ECDSA only. ECDH is a Shor-vulnerable (retroactive/HNDL) capability sitting in the toolchain, unused by the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: No key agreement exists in this codebase's own code paths; X25519 sits in the tree via tweetnacl only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's pre-FIPS-202 SHA-3 variant) is this repo's digest workhorse: EIP-712 domain separators, EIP-2612/EIP-3009 typed-struct hashes, event topics and EIP-1967-style storage slots, computed in the Hardhat test suite via web3.utils.keccak256 and bare keccak256 — mirroring the production contracts. The 5 metadata.json entries are solc's per-source keccak256 content digests recorded in the committed build artifact — provenance data consumed by scripts/hardhat/verifyOnChainBytecode.t

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive test-tooling dependency; no password hashing in the product. Same logical dependency as LIB-ea49d4c1.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 capability via @noble/hashes@1.2.0, a transitive dependency of @noble/curves/ethereum-cryptography under web3 1.10 (keccak/sha256/ripemd/blake modules). The application's own digest use is Keccak-256 via web3; SHA-256 also ships and is actually exercised by the ipfs-only-hash metadata-verification path in scripts. Library capability, no direct application call site on @noble/hashes itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Capability-presence only; the repo's operative hash is Keccak-256, not BLAKE3.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@2.0.4 ships in the web3/ethers keystore path (Web3 secret storage / BIP-3 encrypted JSON wallets). Transitive dev-toolchain dependency; no application call site — the repo's keys are runtime-generated test accounts. scrypt is a memory-hard KDF (Shor-resistant by construction; Grover halves work factor at most), so the A- quantum-safe rating is right.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available and exercised: the operative hash of both the contract layer and the test layer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Capability-presence only; no authenticated encryption in first-party code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 17 sites are the same pattern: Node crypto.randomBytes(32) generates the nonce for EIP-2612 permit and EIP-3009 authorization messages in the test suite (test/v2/GasAbstraction/*, NativeFiatTokenV2_2.behavior, v2_2.behavior, V2Upgrader). Proper CSPRNG; quantum-safety is not applicable to a DRBG. Changeable here if nonces ever need to move to production code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 (2017 release) provides NaCl box/secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305), sign (Ed25519) and hash primitives, present transitively in the web3/hardhat toolchain tree. No application call site — the repo signs with secp256k1 via ethereumjs-util. Ed25519/X25519/NaCl primitives are Shor-vulnerable capabilities sitting in the shipped toolchain; also note the version is 7 years old.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive keystore KDF dependency; same dependency scout 2's scrypt algorithm object (ALG-c1f8b585) is derived from.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js provides streaming SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512. Notably this version is a governance decision, not a default: package.json "resolutions" pins sha.js to 2.4.12 and cipher-base to 1.0.7 explicitly. Transitive dep of the web3/crypto-browserify toolchain; no direct application call site. Capability ships with the test toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md5@2.3.0 is present as a transitive toolchain dependency in the lockfile. MD5 is collision-broken, so it must stay visible in the inventory even though no application call site exists — the shipped product (Solidity bytecode) cannot reach it. If anything in the web3/hardhat tree ever routes through it, the roster's SHA-384 migration applies.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive web3-stack dependency; capability-presence entry. Note: elliptic 6.5.4 predates the 2024 signature-validation fixes (CVE-2024-28802, CVE-2024-42461; fixed in 6.6.x) — the pin is worth upgrading even though no direct use exists.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The hash-primitives library of the shipped tree; Keccak-256 is its exercised export here. ALG-979eccf8 (BLAKE3) and ALG-c9ef78a4 (SHA-3) are its other exports seen from the algorithm side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Elliptic's internal hash dependency; no first-party use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.1.0 is the modern elliptic-curve library under web3's ethereum-cryptography; its secp256k1 module is what the test toolchain would use for Ethereum signature operations. The application-side signing actually goes through ethereumjs-util's ecsign (reported separately), but this library ships the same Shor-vulnerable curve families (secp256k1, P-256, ed25519, x25519) as available capability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same logical dependency as ALG-4de3b020 (the PBKDF2 capability of this package).
